transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 10:15 AM PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Jenny Park, Evan Liu, Priya Nair, Carlos Martinez, Marta Orlov, Samir Gupta
Recorded with Fireflies.ai

Summary (auto): quick staging drill for traffic shaping + fallback policies; verify canary thresholds, KV-cache miss scenarios, and runbook clarity. Decision to run a 72-hour staging experiment and a follow-up table-top on 2026-03-12.

Topics: staging traffic split, fallback model variants, KV cache storm, runbook ownership, rollback escalation path

---Transcript---
[00:00] Alex Chen: alright folks, let's kick off. I think we have most folks, um, thanks for making time on a thursday. The goal today is to run through the traffic shaping strategy and execute a fallback drill in staging so we can catch any surprises before the public rollout.
[00:20] Priya Nair: morning. quick note, i dropped the draft router YAML in the playbook link, it's called traffic-split-v2. there are threshold comments inline.
[00:35] Jenny Park: perfect, thanks. can we also confirm what success looks like for the drill? like latency SLOs versus token cost impact, right?
[00:48] Evan Liu: yea so from runtime side we care about 95th latency staying under 220ms for short calls; for long horizon calls—like 1k tokens—expect higher but percentage wise we can't increase error rate. We also want to measure token-per-infer cost delta when we route to smaller quantized variants.
[01:10] Carlos Martinez: and SLOs are the same as staging SLAs--we'll run a synthetic load with kv cache priming and cold-starts to emulate real prefix diversity. note: last time the kv cache misread as k v cache in the script cause some confusion in logs, so i fixed naming.
[01:30] Priya Nair: nice. quick question, when we say "fallback" are we talking model fallback only or also regional fallback to other clusters?
[01:40] Alex Chen: both. primary plan is model variant fallback — degrade to smaller quantized family — but policy includes region reroute if capacity pressure persists. the two-tier fallback: model -> region.
[01:57] Marta Orlov: i want to call out the escalation path: if we detect token error rate over 0.5% for 2 minutes, oncall gets paged and we immediately flip to model-fallback policy for 10% of traffic as a canary. if that relieves pressure we roll further.
[02:18] Samir Gupta: that paging threshold seems tight, whats the false positive risk during deploy spikes?
[02:27] Jenny Park: good point. we should add deploy window suppression and correlate with our deploy events stream so we don't flip during a deployment artifact surge.
[02:36] Evan Liu: technically we can correlate with the deploy webhook; i'll add an event suppression filter in the alert.
[02:45] Alex Chen: ok let's walk through the staged exercise steps, i'll read them and we can annotate. step one: start synthetic ramp to 40% of expected peak across the US-west cluster for 30 minutes. step two: introduce KV-cache churn pattern at t+15m. step three: trigger model-fallback policy at t+25m for 10% traffic. step four: gauge latency/cost/quality metrics for 15 minutes then decide scale-out or rollback.
[03:18] Priya Nair: i had an ask, can we make the ramp more realistic by adding prefix skew? like 20% of requests with long context and 80% short. otherwise quantized variants behave differently.
[03:32] Evan Liu: yes add the 1k-token path. i'll adjust the load generator. also we'll tag requests so the tracing shows model variant IDs in the logs.
[03:42] Carlos Martinez: transcription note - the LLM model names in the log are sometimes truncated like rdw-7b-q8 -> rdw-seven-b, so when we search logs for model id we should run normalization.
[03:55] Alex Chen: good catch. next, fallback validation: we need quality checks to ensure we don't degrade beyond tolerances — for now quality baseline is 85% pass on the internal eval suite (prompt set A). if fallback variant falls below that, we will not expand fallback beyond 10% without manual signoff.
[04:20] Jenny Park: can we put that eval suite on a nightly job so we have a rolling baseline?
[04:27] Evan Liu: yes, there's already a nightly run for core models, i'll add variants to the matrix.
[04:33] Marta Orlov: for the oncall runbook, do we have a short goto checklist? last time folks scrambled over who toggles router flags.
[04:44] Priya Nair: in the draft runbook (see link) i added the responsibilities: SE oncall toggles model-fallback flag, release eng performs region reroute, and PM owns external comms. but we need to test the toggle permissions in staging.
[05:00] Samir Gupta: question on permissions—who can flip region reroute? that's an infra-level permission, we should limit it to release eng + infra leads only.
[05:10] Alex Chen: agree, we limit it. add a two-person approval for region reroute for safety.
[05:18] Evan Liu: two-person approval is fine, spool up a GH issue that requires approvals, or use the internal ops console with an approval step.
[05:28] Priya Nair: moving on, modeling the cost delta: if we route 20% to q4 quantized variants what is the expected unit cost saving? Evan?
[05:38] Evan Liu: ballpark 15-25% token cost per routed token depending on sequence length. but there's also the overhead of cache misses and possible regen attempts (if quality dips). we need to measure end-to-end cost not just inference cost.
[05:52] Carlos Martinez: that's the tricky bit—cache locality matters. if fallback variants don't share KV layout, regen can double token spend. simulation will capture that.
[06:05] Jenny Park: ok let's pause and sketch the failover timing diagram — Alex can you share screen?
[06:10] [screen share begins, Alex walks through diagram pasted in playbook link]
[06:32] Alex Chen: diagram shows detection -> canary flip -> monitor 15m -> scale or rollback. detection window is 2m with 75% of sampling from 95th percentile lat spikes.
[06:45] Evan Liu: small nit: sampling at 75% of spikes is weird language, we should say sample windowed quantiles and use streaming percentile aggregator.
[06:54] Priya Nair: noted. another scenario—what about partial degradation where certain prompt families break on quantized models but others are fine? we need per-prompt-tag metrics.
[07:08] Marta Orlov: yes we need per-prompt tag SLOs; this is more of an observability investment. we can at least tag the top ten failure prompts and escalate.
[07:20] Samir Gupta: do we have capacity to keep two model families warm simultaneously in staging? cold-starts could skew the experiment.
[07:30] Evan Liu: staging will reserve a small pool for warm variants; we'll pre-warm the KV caches for the smaller family to reduce cold-start noise. pre-warming script will be part of the experiment artifacts.
[07:40] Jenny Park: let's schedule the 72-hour continuous run started Thursday night so we have business hours windows on Friday-Monday to observe.
[07:50] Alex Chen: ok, 72-hour run. who owns the ops to start it? Evan?
[07:56] Evan Liu: i'll own the start and monitoring. Carlos will own the simulation harness.
[08:03] Carlos Martinez: i'll also simulate region outage by adding latency on one AZ to see region reroute behavior.
[08:12] Priya Nair: we also need to test the rollback announcement flow: i.e., if we escalate to manual rollback, who crafts the customer comms? Jenny?
[08:20] Jenny Park: yep i'll draft the templated status message and internal comms. i want a one-pager for execs summarizing metrics and mitigations.
[08:29] Alex Chen: good. quick pause for questions. any concerns about telemetry or noise?
[08:36] Marta Orlov: telemetry retention—do we have enough retention to analyze 72 hours at minute-level granularity?
[08:43] Evan Liu: yes, staging retention is 14 days at minute granularity. we'll pull down raw traces if needed.
[08:50] Samir Gupta: suggested throttle: during the canary flip, we use progressive ramping 10% -> 30% -> 50% if quality holds, rather than jumping.
[09:00] Priya Nair: that's less risky. but set max ramp time to 10 minutes between steps.
[09:08] Alex Chen: agree. next set of notes: we had a previous incident where fallback caused garbled structured output because of deterministic decoding differences — we must include structured-output regression checks in the eval.
[09:25] Evan Liu: right, add structured schema tests. the eval harness will flag schema violations.
[09:31] Jenny Park: is the eval open to product folks to add new prompts easily?
[09:36] Evan Liu: i'll make a small uploader tool for prompt owners. it'll be read-only to avoid polluting the canonical set.
[09:45] Carlos Martinez: misc nit—logs show many mismatched model IDs because of our naming normalization. will centralize normalization mapping in the logging layer.
[09:55] Priya Nair: ok let's run the dry run checklist: permissions checked, pre-warm pools, load generator scripts updated, alert suppression in place, runbook published, comm templates drafted. who is green on each?
[10:09] Evan Liu: runtime + scripts green.
[10:12] Carlos Martinez: simulation harness green after i push the kv churn fixes.
[10:15] Marta Orlov: runbook mostly green, i need to add the exact pager escalation wording.
[10:21] Jenny Park: comm templates green.
[10:24] Priya Nair: router YAML approved pending minor threshold tweak.
[10:29] Alex Chen: ok we have owners for each. we will start the run tonight at 11:00pm PDT. after the run we reconvene in a write-up meeting on 2026-03-12 10:00am to review outcomes and decide go/no-go.
[10:42] Samir Gupta: about decision criteria — i want it explicit: 95th latency <220ms, error rate <0.5%, structured-output pass rate >90% across probes. if any violated, require manual signoff.
[10:56] Jenny Park: agree. i'll put that as the decision bullets in the runbook.
[11:03] Evan Liu: one more thought: in the metrics dashboard let's surface per-model kv-cache hit rate, per-region latency, scaffolded rollback button state and the last transit commit id.
[11:17] Alex Chen: perfect. action wrap-up: Evan runs the experiment, Priya finalizes router YAML, Carlos sim harness, Marta oncall runbook, Jenny comms. reconvene 2026-03-12 for results.
[11:33] Priya Nair: can we also schedule a tabletop for 30 minutes next week to walk through pager flow?
[11:38] Marta Orlov: i'll schedule it for 2026-03-09 9am.
[11:44] Alex Chen: thanks everyone. if no other items, we'll adjourn.
[11:50] End transcript.
